research_scope: Source-free, mathematically type-aware audit of shared prerequisites; no source edits and no broad Batch143 population.

aliases.reason: The topological boundary formula cl_X(A)∩cl_X(X\A) and subspace topology A∩U are instances of the same binary intersection of arbitrary sets. Closure, complement and openness are separate input restrictions of their parent formulas, not properties of the binary intersection operation.

The Rees algebra source forms ⊕_{n≥0}I^n, where each ideal power is an R-module and the direct sum is finite-support external module sum. The generic module-colimit source defines ⊕_iM_i in precisely that manner. Graded multiplication and the ideal-power indexing are additional Rees-algebra structure.

The tensor algebra source forms the external direct sum of its tensor powers M^{⊗n}, which are R-modules. It shares the finite-support module direct-sum construction ⊕_i M_i; tensor powers and concatenation multiplication remain parent-specific.

The irreducible-component definition picks an inclusion-maximal irreducible subset among all irreducible subsets of X. The Noetherian ideal/module sources use the same order-theoretic maximal-member predicate in families ordered by inclusion. Irreducibility and Noetherianity are distinct properties.

Formal smoothness uses an R-algebra A with quotient A/I and canonical algebra map A→A/I for a square-zero ideal I. This contains the ordinary ring quotient construction, already used for I-adic and polynomial quotients. The R-algebra action, I²=0 and the lifting test remain source-specific.
